faq.q: What topic categories are built in?
faq.a: A large library grouped by purpose: school and competitive debate, GD sets for placements and MBA interviews, UPSC essay statements, JAM/extempore one-minute prompts, presentation topics (science, technology, commerce, arts, environment, social issues), project ideas by stream, blog/content ideas, and creative-writing prompts. You pick a category (or 'All categories') and can filter by Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty, which is assigned per category.

Switch Mode to 'No repeats (exclusion list)' and every topic you draw is added to an exclusion list and removed from the pool, so you won't get it again until you click 'Reset exclusions'. You can also set a Pick count from 1 to 20 to draw several distinct topics at once. The pool size and how many you've excluded so far are shown under the result.

It's a JAM/GD-style timer with two phases: a prep time (default 60s) to think, then a speaking time (default 120s). Audible tones generated via the Web Audio API cue the start, the switch from prep to speaking, and completion. When a session finishes it's auto-logged to your history. You can practise the last picked topic, a topic you type in, and see a starter structure of talking points.

faq.q: Can I use my own topic lists and keep a record?
faq.a: Yes. The Custom Lists tab lets you paste topics (one per line) or add them one at a time, name a list, and save it; saved lists appear in the picker and can be exported/imported as JSON. The History tab logs practised topics with date, a 1–5 star self-rating, and notes, and offers a .txt download or a printable practice sheet. Data is stored locally under tp_history and tp_lists.
